source_text: Φησὶν οὖν· τὰ μὲν ὑπὸ τῆς Πυθίας ἢ Δωδωνίδων ἢ Κλαρίου ἢ ἐν Βραγχίδαις ἢ ἐν Ἄμμωνος ὑπὸ μυρίων τε ἄλλων θεοπρόπων προειρημένα, ὑφ᾿ ὧν ἐπιεικῶς πᾶσα γῆ κατῳκίσθη, ταῦτα μὲν (ἐν) οὐδενὶ λόγῳ τίθενται· τὰ δὲ ὑπο τῶν ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ τῷ ἐκείνων τρόπῳ λεχθέντα ἢ μὴ λεχθέντα, καὶ ὥσπερ εἰώθασιν ἔτι νῦν οἱ περὶ Φοινίκην τε καὶ Παλαιστίνην, ταῦτά γε θαυμαστὰ καὶ ἀπαράλλακτα ἡγοῦνται. λέγωμεν οὖν περὶ τῶν κατειλεγμένων χρηστηρίων ὅτι δυνατὸν μὲν ἡμῖν συνάγουσιν ἀπὸ Ἀριστοτέλους καὶ τῶν τὰ τοῦ Περιπάτου φιλοσοφησάντων οὐκ ὀλίγα εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀνατροπὴν τοῦ περὶ τῆς Πυθίας καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν χρηστηρίων λόγου· δυνατὸν δὲ καὶ τὰ λελεγμένα τῷ Ἐπικούρῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀσπαζομένοις αὐτοῦ τὸν λόγον περὶ τῶν αὐτῶν παραθέμενον δεῖξαι ὅτι καὶ Ἑλλήνων τινὲς ἀνατρέπουσι τὰς νομιζομένας καὶ τεθαυμασμένας ἐν πάσῃ Ἑλλάδι θεοπροπίας. ἀλλὰ γὰρ δεδόσθω μὴ εἶναι πλάσματα μηδὲ προσποιήσεις ἀνθρώπων περὶ θεοφορίας τὰ περὶ τὴν Πυθίαν καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ χρηστήρια· ἴδωμεν οὖν εἰ μὴ καὶ οὕτως δύναται τοῖς φιλαλήθως ἐξετάζουσι τὰ πράγματα ἀποδείκνυσθαι ὅτι καὶ τῷ παραδεχομένῳ εἶναι ταῦτα τὰ μαντεῖα οὐκ ἀναγκαῖον προσέσθαι ὅτι θεοί τινες εἰσὶ παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τοῦ ἐναντίου δαίμονές τινες φαῦλοι καὶ πνεύματα ἐχθρὰ τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ κωλύοντα τὴν τῆς ψυχῆς ἄνοδον καὶ δι᾿ ἀρετῆς πορείαν καὶ τῆς ἀληθινῆς εὐσεβείας ἀποκατάστασιν πρὸς τὸν θεόν. ἱστόρηται τοίνυν περὶ τῆς Πυθίας, ὅπερ δοκεῖ τῶν ἄλλων μαντείων λαμπρότερον τυγχάνειν. ὅτι περικαθεζομένη τὸ τῆς Κασταλίας στόμιον ἡ τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος προφῆτις δέχεται πνεῦμα διὰ τῶν γυναικείων κόλπων· οὗ πληρωθεῖσα ἀποφθέγγεται τὰ νομιζόμενα εἶναι σεμνὰ καὶ θεῖα μαντεύματα. ὅρα δὴ διὰ τούτων εἰ μὴ τὸ τοῦ πνεύματος ἐκείνου ἀκάθαρτον καὶ βέβηλον ἐμφαίνεται, μὴ διὰ μανῶν καὶ ἀφανῶν πόρων καὶ πολλῷ γυναικείων κόλπων καθαρωτέρων ἐπεισιὸν τῇ ψυχῇ τῆς θεσπιζούσης ἀλλὰ διὰ τούτων, ἃ οὐδὲ θέμις ἦν τῷ σώφρονι καὶ ἀνθρώπῳ βλέπειν, οὔπω λέγεσθαι ἢ καὶ ἅπτεσθαι· καὶ τοῦτο ποιεῖν οὐχ ἅπαξ που οὐδὲ δὶς (ἴσως γὰρ ἔδοξεν ἀνεκτότερον τὸ τοιοῦτο τυγχάνειν), ἀλλὰ τοσαυτάκις, ὁσάκις προφητεύειν ἐκείνη ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος πεπίστευται. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ εἰς ἔκστασιν καὶ μανικὴν ἄγειν κατάστασιν τὴν δῆθεν προφητεύουσαν, ὡς μηδαμῶς αυτὴν ἑαυτῇ παρακολουθεῖν, οὐ θείου πνεύματος ἔργον ἐστίν· ἐχρῆν γὰρ τὸν κάτοχον τῷ θείῳ πνεύματι πολλῷ πρότερον παντὸς οὑτινοσοῦν τοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν χρησμῶν διδασκομένου τὸ συμβαλλόμενον εἰς τὸν μέσον καὶ κατὰ φύσιν βίον ἢ πρὸς τὸ λυσιτελὲς ἢ πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον ὠφεληθῆναι καὶ διορατικώτερον παρ᾿ ἐκεῖνο μάλιστα καιροῦ τυγχάνειν, ὅτε σύνεστιν αὐτῷ τὸ θεῖον.
pass_a_gloss: He says then: the things spoken by the Pythia or the Dodonian or the Clarian or in Branchidae or in Ammon by thousands of other prophets, by whom the whole earth was inhabited in a gentle manner, these things are not considered in any word; but the things spoken by those in Judea in their manner, or not spoken, and as those around Phoenicia and Palestine are accustomed even now, these things they consider wonderful and unchanging. Let us say then concerning the oracles that have been mentioned, that it is possible for us to gather from Aristotle and those who philosophized in the Peripatetic manner not a few things to overturn the word concerning the Pythia and the other oracles; it is possible also to show the things said by Epicurus and those who welcome his word concerning the same things, that some Greeks also overturn the prophetic things that are considered and marveled at in all of Greece. But if it is granted that the things concerning the Pythia and the other oracles are not fabrications or human pretenses concerning divine inspiration, let us see if it is possible to demonstrate to those who examine things in a love of truth that even if one accepts that these are oracles, it is not necessary to agree that some gods are present, but rather that some evil demons and hostile spirits to the human race, hindering the ascent of the soul and the journey through virtue and the restoration of true piety towards God. It is reported then concerning the Pythia, which seems to be more renowned than the other oracles, that sitting around the mouth of Castalia, the prophetess of Apollo receives a spirit through the female organs; having been filled with this, she utters the things that are considered to be solemn and divine prophecies. See then through these things if the unclean and profane nature of that spirit is not revealed, not entering the soul of the prophetess through pure and invisible channels, and much cleaner than the female organs, but through these things, which it was not even lawful for a sane and human person to see or touch; and this is done not just once or twice (for perhaps such a thing seemed more tolerable), but as many times as she is believed to prophesy from Apollo. But also the fact that the supposed prophetess is led into an ecstatic and manic state, so that she is not following herself, is not the work of a divine spirit; for the one possessed by the divine spirit ought to have been benefited much earlier by all that is taught through the oracles, and to have been more discerning, especially at the time when the divine is present to him.
pass_b_english: He goes on to say that the pronouncements uttered by the Pythia, the Dodonian priests, the Clarian oracle, the shrine at Branchidae, the oracle of Ammon, and by thousands of other prophets — through whom the whole earth was gently settled — are not given any credence at all. Yet the things spoken by those in Judea in the same fashion, or even things that were never spoken, and the sort of utterances still customary today among the peoples of Phoenicia and Palestine, these they regard as marvelous and unalterable.

Let us then address the oracles that have been cited. We can collect from Aristotle and the philosophers of the Peripatetic school plenty of arguments to overturn the case for the Pythia and the other oracles. We can also adduce the statements of Epicurus and his followers on the same subject to show that even some Greeks reject the prophetic claims that are revered and wondered at throughout Greece.

But suppose we grant that the phenomena surrounding the Pythia and the other oracles are not fabrications or human pretenses of divine inspiration. Let us see whether, even on that concession, one can demonstrate to those who investigate honestly that accepting these utterances as genuine oracles does not compel us to acknowledge the presence of gods. On the contrary, they point to evil demons and spirits hostile to the human race, beings that obstruct the soul's ascent, the path of virtue, and the restoration of true piety toward God.

The Pythia is reported to be the most renowned of the oracles. She sits over the mouth of the Castalian spring, and the prophetess of Apollo receives a spirit through her female organs; filled with it, she delivers what are taken to be solemn and divine prophecies. Consider whether this does not reveal the unclean and profane character of that spirit. It does not enter the prophetess's soul through pure, invisible channels — channels far cleaner than the female organs — but through parts that it is not even lawful for a sane person to look at or touch. And this happens not merely once or twice (for perhaps that might seem more tolerable), but as often as she is believed to prophesy from Apollo.

Moreover, driving the supposed prophetess into an ecstatic, manic state in which she loses all self-possession is not the work of a divine spirit. The one indwelt by the divine Spirit ought to have been benefited long before by everything taught through the oracles, and to have become more discerning — most of all at the very moment when the divine is present to him.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the complex conditional structures and the specific list of oracles. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source. The distinction between the 'unclean' nature of the spirit and the 'pure' channels is preserved. The theological argument regarding the soul's ascent and the nature of the divine spirit is correctly rendered.
